components: ShortLinkEndpoints (minimal API routing, rate-limit and header handling)
ShortenerService (create, resolve, deactivate, metadata, analytics orchestration)
UrlValidator (scheme allowlist, userinfo, length, localhost/private/loopback/link-local IP blocking incl. IPv4-mapped IPv6)
CodeGenerator/Base62 (7-char unique codes with collision retry)
OwnerToken service (128+ bit RNG token, SHA-256 hash stored, CryptographicOperations.FixedTimeEquals)
ShortenerOptions (rate limit, max expiry days, max URL length)
Program/AppHost (DI wiring, JSON error handling to 400)

endpoints.summary: Create short link with optional alias and expiry; returns code, shortUrl, expiresAt, ownerToken and Location header
Redirect (302) to target; counts click on success only
Existing legacy stats route, kept working

dataModel: ShortLink: Code (string, case-sensitive key), TargetUrl, CreatedAt, ExpiresAt?, IsActive, OwnerTokenHash (byte[]/SHA-256, never exposed)
risks: Hostnames resolving to private IPs are not blocked (no DNS check); documented residual SSRF/open-redirect risk, service never fetches targets
In-memory store loses data on restart and is single-instance only
Fixed-window limiter allows bursts at window boundaries and needs stale-entry cleanup to bound memory
Rate limiting by remote IP is inaccurate behind proxies unless forwarded headers are explicitly configured
Alias vs generated code collisions: generated codes must retry against the shared keyspace; atomic TryAdd needed to avoid races
Existing code may already implement parts; gaps must be verified against each acceptance criterion (e.g. IPv4-mapped IPv6, 365-day cap, 429 counting of 400/409)
Legacy GET /{code} could shadow or conflict with reserved aliases and other routes

decisions.rationale: Meets scope and latency target; persistence can be added later
decisions.alternative: Database such as SQLite now (more scope, slower tests)

decisions.decision: Rate limiter applied before validation so 400/409 also count
decisions.rationale: FR-8 requires rejected requests to count; GET redirects are excluded

decisions.decision: Store SHA-256 hash of 128+ bit random token, compare with FixedTimeEquals
decisions.rationale: High-entropy token makes fast hash sufficient and avoids timing leaks
decisions.alternative: Slow password hash (unnecessary for random tokens)

decisions.decision: Literal IP/localhost blocking only, parsing IPv4-mapped IPv6 and normalizing hosts
decisions.rationale: Matches assumption; service never fetches target
decisions.alternative: DNS resolution check (TOCTOU, latency, still bypassable via rebinding)

decisions.decision: 302 redirect with Interlocked click increment only after successful resolve
decisions.rationale: Expiry and deactivation take effect immediately; exact concurrent counts

decisions.decision: Return 403 for invalid owner token and 401 for missing
Retain legacy routes /{code} and /stats as aliases of canonical handlers

impact.reason: Verify/adjust routes, status codes, Location header, rate-limit placement, X-Owner-Token handling, JSON 400 handling
Ensure response shapes include required fields and exclude token hash
Create/resolve/deactivate logic, expiry 365-day cap, idempotent delete, constant-time token check
Scheme allowlist, userinfo, length, private/loopback/link-local/mapped IP blocking
Per-IP counters, Retry-After, configurable limits, cleanup
Record clicks only on successful redirects
Atomic add for alias uniqueness, case-sensitive keys

dataFlows: Create: client -> rate limiter (per IP) -> JSON bind -> UrlValidator/AliasValidator/expiry check -> code generation or alias -> token generate+hash -> repository atomic add -> 201 with token
Redirect: client -> resolve code -> check exists/active/unexpired -> ClickRecorder Interlocked increment -> 302 Location
Deactivate: client + X-Owner-Token -> hash+FixedTimeEquals -> set IsActive=false -> 204
Analytics: client -> repository existence check -> AnalyticsStore snapshot -> 200
